test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A tap fills a cistern in 18 hours. Another tap empties the full tank in 19 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill one-third of the tank, if the tank is empty initially and both the taps are open together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net efficiency for filling the tank = 1/18 − 1/19 = 1/342 part per hour.

Time to fill the **full tank** = 342 hours.

Time to fill **one-third** of the tank = 342 ÷ 3 = 114 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 114 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Filling Tap** time = 18 hours

**Emptying Tap** time = 19 hours

**Target:** Fill 1/3 of the tank capacity.

 
 **Tap Type** **Time (hr)** **Total Work (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 Inlet (+) 18 342 units +19 
 Outlet (−) 19 −18 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total capacity of the cistern = **LCM**(18, 19) = 342 units.

⇒ Net efficiency of both taps = 19 − 18 = 1 unit/hour.

⇒ Target volume to be filled = 1/3 × 342 = 114 units.

⇒ Time required = Target Volume ÷ Net Efficiency

⇒ Time required = 114 ÷ 1 = 114 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 114 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

Efficiency of an **Inlet pipe** is always positive, while the efficiency of an **Outlet (leakage) pipe** is taken as negative.

Total Work Concept

Total capacity or work is usually the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the individual times taken by each pipe.

Combined Rate Formula

If pipe A fills in 'x' hours and pipe B empties in 'y' hours, net rate per hour is (1/x − 1/y). Tank fills only if x < y.</p
